finding.claim: The avatar endpoint fetches a user-supplied URL. The only check is a startswith('https://') prefix, so any https host is allowed, including internal hosts, cloud metadata proxies and localhost. Axios follows redirects by default, so an attacker-hosted https URL can 302 to http://169.254.169.254/ or http://users.internal:8080/. There is no host or IP allow-list or deny-list and no DNS pinning.

trace.note: only checks typeof string and startsWith('https://')
axios.get(url) is called with the raw URL; redirects are followed by default (maxRedirects 5)
the response size is returned to the caller, which gives a blind or semi-blind oracle (the response size is returned)

finding.guards_checked: The https:// prefix check is the only guard. It does not restrict the host, resolve or check IPs, or disable redirects. https://internal-host/, https://127.0.0.1:port and https://[::1]/ all pass. Redirects to http:// targets are not blocked.

verdict.guard_found: none (only typeof string and startsWith('https://') at server.js:11; no auth middleware, host allow-list, IP check, or maxRedirects restriction)
verdict.reason: server.js:10 takes req.body.avatarUrl, server.js:11 only checks the https:// prefix, and server.js:14 passes it to axios.get with default redirect following, so internal hosts are reachable and server.js:15 returns the byte length as an oracle.
